proposal.title: Azure agent-assist for synthetic support calls (first concrete sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: inbound synthetic call → consent gate → real-time transcription → PII redaction → grounded suggestions to a human agent → agent-approved summary and CRM draft. The system never makes outbound calls or writes to the CRM. The agent copies the approved draft into the existing CRM themselves. Assumptions: region not chosen; service availability, model access and quotas not checked; Terraform generator coverage for these Azure services is not native, so engineering is required. Local tests use mocked speech, PII and model behaviour only.

response.message: The emulation found no failing checks. The design holds together: every flow is connected, consent is checked before transcription, and the CRM step stays manual. It is still blocked because no supported generator covers the Azure parts yet: call intake, consent, Speech, Language PII, the orchestrator, AI Search and Azure OpenAI. The synthetic caller also has no reference plan. None of these blocks fit an existing typed contract without cutting scope, so I'm leaving the board unchanged. The fix is product engineering work: native Azure implementations, using this artifact (73895101…) and revision 2 to reproduce the problem. After that, we rerun emulation on a new artifact. While that work happens, let's settle a decision that only you can make, because it fixes where Speech, Language and the OpenAI model can run: which country must the call audio and transcripts stay in?
